# PR 293 correctness review: round 2, final under C34

## Verdict

PASS WITH NOTES. P293-001 is closed for the ordinary, killable tmux IPC client.
F244 is the prime's named residual, folded into the F243 PR; it does not block
this final review or start a third round. The reviewer/293 holding remains
until merge.

## Repair and disposition

Reviewed only d17dae35..0a7ff6de: two commits, three files. The original HTTP
drain and control-release implementation did not change.

At justfile:749-792, the setter is launched with stdin/stdout on /dev/null
and stderr in the private build-copy directory. The SECONDS-based wait lasts
1-2 seconds plus scheduling/poll overhead; on expiry only the owned setter PID
is killed and waited for. Timeout and unexpected command failure refuse before
SIGINT. Success and the recognized no-server/no-socket/no-session diagnostics
proceed. Exactly PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE=1 explicitly overrides the refusal and emits
its diagnostic.

The error message accurately says the new binary has already been installed:
the old daemon is left running, not every deployment side effect rolled back.
The protection/refusal is a brake on stopping the old daemon, not retention.

The permanent recipe tests run the actual Bash body, not a reimplementation.
They prove both normal/name-selected argv, protection before the stop,
recognized benign failures, timeout refusal, permission-denied refusal and
the explicit unsafe override. Their victim is an owned real sleep process;
tmux, build, installation and port probes are fakes. The shebang-aware harness
change also preserves the existing stamp/install/nudge tests.

## Named residual and proof ceilings

- F244: when command -v tmux fails, the inherited no-else branch still reaches
  SIGINT without protection or PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE=1. A signal-free probe of the
  exact helper, PATH=/var/empty and UNSAFE unset, returned rc 0 and reached
  the stop marker. No real daemon or tmux server was touched.
  The prime's C34 ruling, relayed by pm-001, explicitly accepts this as F244
  folded into the F243 PR. That follow-up should refuse missing tmux unless
  overridden, or resolve it as the daemon does.
- The wait after SIGKILL has no independent timer. This proof establishes
  ordinary killable-child cleanup, not an absolute bound on OS-level
  uninterruptible/reaping failure. Performance routed that qualification to
  the PM; it is not a newly invented third-round gate.
- Native -L/default resolution replaced synthesized -S. The argv tests pass;
  the security holder owns the socket/old-environment security verdict.
- The inherited CLI tail EOF exit is already a named known limit. No unchanged
  stream/client behavior was re-reviewed or re-tested here.
- No additional mutation runs or real-tmux smoke were performed in this round.
  The coder's mutation/smoke claims remain attributed to the packet, not to
  this reviewer's direct evidence. Two postmerge production bounces remain
  prime-owned and are not supplied by these tests.
